catalog.summary: Typed time input split into segments.

patternStatus: Read on 2026-09-10 and transcribed key by key The example the pattern links is deprecated for its visible increment and decrement buttons; its roles, its wrapping rule and its aria-valuetext guidance are taken whole and the buttons are not drawn.
zonedReason: A zoned instant is the type every surveyed implementation gets wrong at a daylight boundary: holding one would owe an answer for the hour that happens twice and the hour that never happens. What this library holds is the wall-clock value the reader typed, and converting it is the application's, against the zone the application knows. Decided in wave 7 and recorded in docs/build-briefing.md.

engine.widened: SegmentState gains hour, minute, second and dayPeriod; the reference parameter gains the same four and the hour cycle, all optional, so every date-field call site compiles unchanged; fieldRange gains four rows and an hourCycle. The engine steps a number inside a range, wraps it, takes typed digits and ends a run when no further digit fits, and it does not know what a field means.
engine.why: A second engine would be one behavior corrected in two places, and datetime-field needs one SegmentState holding both halves — two states side by side would make "the reader is typing" two questions with two answers.

hourCycleReason: Intl resolves four cycles and a boolean can say two. ja-JP writes midnight as hour zero under h11, and a family that stores 12 there is wrong in a way nobody notices until a Japanese reader reports it. The public axis stays 12 | 24, because that is the question a consumer asks; which variant of each the locale writes is the locale's.

dayPeriod.typedBy: the first letter of the locale name
dayPeriod.drawnWhen: the resolved hour cycle is h11 or h12
dayPeriod.why: Two values in a range is a spin button, so ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home and End need no special case. aria-valuenow is 0 or 1, which is not user-friendly, and the pattern names aria-valuetext as the answer.

keyboard.matches: the first letter of a locale name

departures.pageStep: The APG spin-button example steps every button by five. Fifteen minutes is the page a reader of a time field means and the step a quarter-hour panel offers, so the two agree; three hours is a quarter of a twelve-hour cycle. The cost is a reader who learned five from another spin button on the same page and finds this one moves further.
departures.noArrowButtons: The example the pattern links is deprecated for its visible increment and decrement buttons, which duplicate keys the reader already has. Its roles, its wrapping rules and its aria-valuetext guidance are the spin-button pattern's and are taken whole. No arrow buttons are drawn.
departures.arrowsAcross: The pattern has no key for moving between spin buttons, because its example holds one. ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move between the fields and are logical rather than physical: in a right-to-left document the arrow that walks forward is the one pointing along the writing direction. The cost is that a reader who expects the caret behavior of a text input finds a whole field moving instead.
departures.relativeKeys: +, - and = are not printable characters the value can hold, and the pattern says any other character does not change the value. They open a second entry mode instead. The cost is a reader who types + expecting nothing and gets an expression; the mode is abandoned whole by Escape, and relative={false} removes it.

entryModel.runEndsWhen: the segment is full, or one more digit could not fit under its maximum
entryModel.requestEmittedOn: the end of a run, never inside one
entryModel.keysAreConsumed: a key the field acts on is stopped, not only defaulted
entryModel.whyKeysAreConsumed: Every application that binds a bare key guards it with "is the target an editable element", and that guard tests for input, textarea and contenteditable. A div with role=spinbutton is none of the three, so a reader typing a time fires every single-key shortcut on the page. preventDefault does not help: a shortcut handler reads the key, not the default. Recorded first by date-field and inherited unchanged.
entryModel.whyRequestWaits: Typing 23 into an hour passes through 2, and 2 is a time the arithmetic accepts and nobody meant. The segments move on every keystroke and the value moves when the run ends: on the digit that fills the field, on the key that leaves it, or on blur.
entryModel.wraps: inside the segment, never carrying into the next
entryModel.clearedSegment: the placeholder, and the value becomes null

relative.anchor: now, or referenceTime when the consumer states one
relative.whyNow: One rule, stated once. Resolving against the value the field already holds would make + mean two different things depending on whether the field is empty, and the brief this answers says "a duration from now".
relative.commitsOn: Enter, or blur when the expression resolves
relative.abandonsOn: Escape, or blur when it does not

grammar.sign: + by default, - for a time already past
grammar.bareNumber: minutes, which is the unit a booking flow asks in and the unit step is written in
grammar.compound: 1h30 and 1:30 are both an hour and a half
grammar.localeWords: not parsed. The grammar is symbols and unit letters because those are what a numeric keyboard offers in every locale, and daqui a 40 minutos would work in one language and none of the others. The placeholder states the grammar.

preview.shows: the time the expression resolves to, before anything commits
preview.whyLive: The reader is being asked to accept a value they did not write, so the value has to be perceivable before Enter — including to a reader who cannot see it.

relative.midnight: +90m at 23:00 resolves to 00:30, which is a different day. The preview carries data-crosses-midnight, the announcement names it, and the request carries crossesMidnight so a consumer holding a PlainDateTime beside this field knows to add one. No surveyed implementation says anything at all.
reachableWithout: the arrow keys on every segment
the now control at the head of time-picker's panel

dataAttributes.data-field: which of hour, minute, second or dayPeriod a segment holds
dataAttributes.data-placeholder: the segment has no value and is drawing its placeholder
dataAttributes.data-cycle: 12 or 24, so a stylesheet can size the row that holds a day period
dataAttributes.data-relative: an expression is open in place of the segments
dataAttributes.data-crosses-midnight: the expression resolved into the next day
dataAttributes.data-resolved: the preview holds a time the expression resolves to

literals.--slotted-time-field-segment-min-inline-: A segment is sized from the widest digit its field can hold, which is arithmetic over the control type scale rather than a literal; the floor under the whole control is --slotted-control-height-*, which the theme owns.
literals.--slotted-time-field-period-min-inline-s: The day-period part is sized from the widest of the two names the locale actually writes, measured in ch against the control's own type, because es-MX writes a.m. and a locale may write a word.
